1. Core Clinical Tension: A 57-year-old man from southern Brazil presented with headache, a focal motor seizure, and left homonymous hemianopia. Brain MRI revealed a 5.0-cm solitary parietal ring-enhancing mass with extensive surrounding vasogenic edema, highly suggestive of a primary central nervous system malignancy (high-grade glioma) or metastatic disease. Furthermore, the infection was complicated by co-existing pulmonary strongyloidiasis alongside disseminated fungal disease.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission clinical encounter ends following outpatient neurological evaluation, brain MRI showing the 5.0-cm ring-enhancing parietal lesion, and preoperative chest radiography revealing bilateral micro-nodules and apical emphysema, immediately prior to craniotomy, intraoperative biopsy, and bronchoscopy.
3. Differential Distinctions: High-grade glioma or intracranial abscess was the working diagnosis based on the solitary 5-cm mass with ring-enhancement and edema, but ruled out by craniotomy biopsy showing typical fungal yeast forms without malignancy. Cryptococcal meningoencephalitis was ruled out by negative serum and CSF cryptococcal antigen tests. Tuberculosis was ruled out by negative acid-fast smear. Definitive diagnosis was established by histopathology demonstrating large thick-walled yeast cells with multiple peripheral buds ('mariner's wheel') of Paracoccidioides brasiliensis, and bronchoalveolar lavage confirming P. brasiliensis yeasts alongside Strongyloides stercoralis larvae.
case_prompt:
A 57-year-old man presented to a tertiary neurosurgery outpatient clinic in Porto Alegre, southern Brazil, with complaints of progressive headache and an episode of a focal motor seizure that had occurred 1 month earlier.

On neurological examination, no gross focal deficits were elicited except for a left homonymous hemianopia on confrontation visual field testing. Cranial nerves, motor strength, sensory modalities, and cerebellar functions were otherwise intact.

Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain demonstrated an expansive, relatively well-defined mass measuring 5.0 cm in diameter in the right parietal lobe. The lesion was isointense on T1-weighted images and heterogeneously hypointense on T2-weighted images, exhibiting intense peripheral ring contrast enhancement with extensive surrounding vasogenic edema suggestive of a primary neoplasm. Preoperative chest radiography revealed multiple bilateral micro-nodules with apical emphysema bullae. Serologic testing for HIV antibodies was negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Primary central nervous system neoplasm (High-grade glioma / Glioblastoma)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary provisional diagnosis based on adult-onset focal seizure, progressive headache, left hemianopia, and brain MRI showing a solitary 5.0-cm mass with peripheral ring-enhancement and extensive vasogenic edema; ruled out during surgery and biopsy, which showed a firm granulomatous lesion containing large yeast cells without malignant cytology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The mass measured 5.0 cm in diameter, showing peripheral contrast enhancement with peri-lesional vasogenic edema suggestive of a primary neoplasm... On anatomo-pathological examination, the findings were pathognomonic of PCM: large, thick-walled, spherical yeast cells with multiple peripheral buds, with the capsule wall thickness giving the impression of a double capsule, although it was a single capsule [Figure 2a and b].

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered intraoperatively when gross inspection revealed a yellowish hard lesion with thick purulent content; ruled out by negative Gram stain and lack of bacterial growth, with demonstration of fungal morphology on pathology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The patient underwent craniotomy and the intraoperative finding was a yellowish, hard lesion with good cleavage plane, thick content, and yellow inside. There was a hypothesis of brain abscess.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given the fungal nature of the lesion and bilateral nodular pulmonary findings; ruled out by negative cryptococcal antigen testing in both serum and cerebrospinal fluid.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) specimens were negative for cryptococcal antigen by the cryptococcal latex agglutination test (Crypto-LA; Wampole Laboratories, Cranbury, NJ, USA).

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Disseminated Paracoccidioidomycosis with CNS pseudotumoral involvement and co-existing Strongyloidiasis (Soil-Transmitted Helminths)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Anatomopathological examination of the excised parietal lesion demonstrated pathognomonic large spherical yeast cells with multiple peripheral buds characteristic of Paracoccidioides brasiliensis ('pilot's wheel' appearance); bronchoalveolar lavage confirmed P. brasiliensis yeast cells alongside Strongyloides stercoralis larvae, establishing disseminated paracoccidioidomycosis with soil-transmitted helminth co-infection.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: On anatomo-pathological examination, the findings were pathognomonic of PCM: large, thick-walled, spherical yeast cells with multiple peripheral buds, with the capsule wall thickness giving the impression of a double capsule, although it was a single capsule [Figure 2a and b]... Analysis of cells obtained from RUL broncho-alveolar lavage (BAL) fluid showed a negative smear for acid-fast bacilli (AFB), negative Gram stain, and presence of Strongyloides stercoralis larvae and yeast cells compatible with P. brasiliensis.

editor_comments: Pseudotumoral neuroparacoccidioidomycosis is an unusual presentation of Paracoccidioides brasiliensis that mimics high-grade intracranial neoplasms. Concomitant opportunistic soil-transmitted helminthiasis (Strongyloides stercoralis) highlights the potential for multiple endemic infections in Latin American patients.
